Filed by s527b (2026-10-31, s530) from the WIDE emission-ab of t/op/incfilter.t:262-276.

`do sub { ... }` (an anonymous sub, no attributes) is lowered as a CALL of the sub: `(funcall (p-anon-sub ...))`.  perl 5.40.3 reads it as `do EXPR` with a CODE ref -- the /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3 /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3-hook / source-filter form incfilter.t tests -- and the call's value is not the do's value.

    my @l = ('$::v = 42;');
    my $r = do sub { return 0 unless @l; $_ = shift @l; return 1 };
    print "1 r=", (defined $r ? $r : "undef"), " v=", ($::v // "undef"), "\n";

perl: `1 r=undef v=undef`; main and the s527b tree: `1 r=1 v=undef` (silent wrong, PRE-EXISTING).  With an attribute (`do sub :lvalue { ... }`) the s527b tree takes the ordinary `(p-do (p-__pcl_set_attributes ...))` path and prints `r=undef` like perl -- on main the label repair turned it into the unattributed spelling.  So the two spellings now lower differently; ONE place decides (find where `do` + an anon-sub literal becomes a funcall -- the DECIDED `do SUBNAME(LIST)` ruling (#158) is about a NAMED sub and does not cover this).  t/op/incfilter.t aborts earlier on Filter::Util::Call (snapshot C_ok 0), so no row moves today.  Probe: scratch/s527b/p7.pl in worktree agent-a743b493df5814081.


=== DONE (s530a, 2026-10-31) ===
PROBED TABLE (perl 5.40.3, scratch/s530a/pr/d1.pl d2.pl d3.pl d4.pl): `do sub { ... }`, `do(sub { ... })`, `do $coderef`, `do [1]` are all do FILE on the reference's string: undef in scalar context, ONE undef in list context, $! = ENOENT, the sub NEVER called; `do sub { ... }->()` is do FILE of the call's value; `eval sub { ... }` is eval STRING of "CODE(0x...)": undef, $@ set, the sub never called; do BLOCK unchanged (`do { sub { 6 } }` returns the code ref).  The task's incfilter-shaped repro reads `r=undef v=undef` in perl.
MECHANISM: PExpr makes the BLOCK of `do {}` a func_ref node, and an anonymous-sub literal is a func_ref too; ExprToCL's do arm (and eval's twin arm) called ANY func_ref.
FIX (Pl/PExpr.pm + Pl/ExprToCL.pm): PExpr marks the do-BLOCK's func_ref (`block_arg`); the do and eval arms call only a marked func_ref, so a sub literal takes the generic do FILE / eval STRING tail like `do $coderef` always did.  An attributed `do sub :lvalue {...}` already took that path.
GUARD: Pl/t/misc-fixes-01.t row 29 (d3 + d4, inverse-verified on 0fb05a79).  corpus-diff vs 0fb05a79 IDENTICAL.
